steps.body: Division is the same fraction rule you've always used: **keep, change, flip**. Keep the first, change ÷ to ·, flip the second. (x/(x+1)) ÷ (x/(x+3)) = (x/(x+1)) · ((x+3)/x) = **(x + 3)/(x + 1)** after the x's cancel.

options.label: (x + 2)/5 · 10/(x − 1)
options.feedback: Right — keep, change, flip the SECOND fraction.

options.label: 5/(x + 2) · 10/(x − 1)
options.feedback: Only the DIVISOR flips — the first fraction is kept as-is.

options.label: (x + 2)/5 · (x − 1)/10
options.feedback: The flip is the whole point: dividing BY (x−1)/10 means multiplying by its reciprocal 10/(x−1).

options.label: (x + 2)/10 · 5/(x − 1)
options.feedback: The 5 stays under the first fraction; the second flips whole: 10 over (x − 1).

steps.body: Chart what the division left behind.

widget.prompt: The quotient reduces to 2(x + 2)/(x − 1). Mark each interval's sign — and notice which x the chart has to exclude.
widget.successFeedback: Positive, negative, positive — with a root at −2 and a wall at 1. Trace where that wall came from: nothing in the original numerator forbids x = 1. It was the DIVISOR, (x − 1)/10, that could not be zero, and flipping it to multiply moved x − 1 underneath the bar. Restrictions come from the operation you performed, not only from the fractions you started with.
widget.crossFeedback: Both cuts are single factors — x + 2 above the bar and x − 1 below — and a single factor flips the sign from either side of it. Each cut changes exactly one sign.
widget.bounceFeedback: Holding a sign across a cut needs an even power there. Each factor here appears once, so the sign really does flip at −2 and again at 1.

predict.prompt: Dividing by (x − 1)/10 bans one value of x. Where does that ban show up in the ANSWER, 2(x + 2)/(x − 1)?

options.label: As a wall at x = 1 that the curve never reaches
Nowhere — the division is finished, so its condition is spent

predict.reveal: You may never divide by zero, so x = 1 was excluded the moment the division was written — and after the flip that factor sits in the denominator, where it shows as a vertical wall. The condition does not expire when the operation is carried out; it is recorded in the result.

steps.body: After the flip, it's Chapter 2 Lesson 1: factor and cancel. (x² − 4)/(x + 3) ÷ (x − 2)/(x + 3) → flip → ((x−2)(x+2)/(x+3)) · ((x+3)/(x−2)) = **x + 2**. Both (x + 3) and (x − 2) cancel across.

explanationVariants: Flip: (x²−4)/(x+3) · (x+3)/(x−2); factor and cancel both pairs — x + 2 remains.

commonBuilds.feedback: (x − 2) is the factor that cancels post-flip — the survivor from x² − 4 is (x + 2).
The flip puts one (x + 3) on TOP — they cancel, they don't stack.
That multiplies WITHOUT flipping — division inverts the second fraction first.

widget.missFeedback: Flip the divisor to (x + 3)/(x − 2), factor x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2), then cancel both pairs.
widget.successFeedback: Right — after the flip, (x + 3) and (x − 2) both cancel.

widget.prompt: Check with x = 3: (x² − 4)/(x + 3) ÷ (x − 2)/(x + 3) should equal 3 + 2. Compute it directly.

commonErrors.feedback: 5/6 ÷ 1/6 = 5/6 · 6 = 5 — flip the divisor instead of multiplying straight across.

explanationVariants: A bare divisor is over 1 — flip it to 1-over.

commonBuilds.feedback: That MULTIPLIES by x — dividing by x means multiplying by 1/x.
It can — factor the top: x(x + 3)/(4x), and the x's cancel to (x + 3)/4.
Dividing by x isn't erasing one exponent everywhere — factor x out: x(x + 3), then cancel.

widget.missFeedback: Dividing by x multiplies by 1/x — factor the top as x(x + 3) and cancel the x's.
widget.successFeedback: Right — x flips to 1/x, and the factored x(x + 3) loses its x.

explanationVariants: The divisor's NUMERATOR becomes a denominator after the flip — its zeros join the banned list: x = 2 here.
Three bans for (anything) ÷ (x − 2)/(x + 3): x = −3 (original bottoms) and x = 2 (flipped).

widget.prompt: When dividing BY (x − 2)/(x + 3), which value becomes newly excluded because of the flip?

options.label: x = 2
options.feedback: Right — the divisor itself is ZERO at x = 2, and dividing by zero is banned; post-flip, (x − 2) sits underneath.

options.label: x = −3
options.feedback: −3 was ALREADY excluded (it's a denominator before the flip) — the NEW ban is the divisor's zero, x = 2.

options.label: x = 3
options.feedback: x = 3 makes the divisor 1/6 — perfectly divisible; the danger is where the divisor is 0: x = 2.

options.label: nothing new
options.feedback: Dividing by zero includes dividing by a ZERO-VALUED fraction — the divisor dies at x = 2, so 2 is banned.

explanationVariants: Both (x + 4) and (x + 1) cancel after the flip.

commonBuilds.feedback: (x + 1) cancels away after the flip — the survivor from x² − 1 is (x − 1).
The flip lifts one (x + 4) to the TOP — the pair cancels rather than stacking below.
That skipped the flip — dividing multiplies by the RECIPROCAL of the second fraction.

widget.missFeedback: Flip the divisor to (x + 4)/(x + 1), factor x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1), then cancel the (x + 4) and (x + 1) pairs.
widget.successFeedback: Right — flip, factor x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1), cancel both pairs.

steps.body: Keep, change, flip — then the multiplication pipeline takes over.
takeaways: Only the divisor flips; the first fraction is kept.
The divisor's numerator zeros become NEW exclusions.
steps.teaser: Next: mixed products and quotients with full restriction bookkeeping.

concept.body: The numeric skeleton: (1/2) ÷ (3/4) = (1/2) · (4/3) = 4/6 = 2/3. Same move with expressions.

explanationVariants: The x's cancel after the flip; 5 over 3 remains.

options.feedback: Right — flip to (5/x), and the x's cancel.
The SECOND fraction flips, sending its 5 to the top: 5/3.

options.label: x²/15
options.feedback: That multiplies without flipping — division inverts the divisor first.

options.label: 5x/3x... unsimplifiable
options.feedback: 5x/3x DOES simplify — the x's are factors and cancel: 5/3.
